note: Long-video sharded random walk, on the profile the Tokyo coverage episode was recorded and accepted with: the road network is whatever region has the longest centreline, NOT the built-up core. Core confinement was tried and abandoned - on four maps measured end to end it needed a 60 cm body clearance, a 120 cm corridor and a reroute loop to pass its gates, and delivered a fraction of the footage. This profile is the one with a passing episode behind it.
family_note: coverage_walk IS the random walk. coverage.py:coverage_walk takes a random unwalked road at each junction rather than solving route inspection, and prepare_walks chains one pass into the next from where the last ended. A separate random_walk family would have been a second copy of the same traversal.
action_mix_note: coverage_tokyo_stroll's bands verbatim. Achieved there: forward 31.9%, backward 16.5%, turn 14.4/13.6%, look 8.6/9.4%, hold 5.6%, in band. The floors sum to 0.67, so the bands are jointly satisfiable.
camera_note: pitch_limit_up_deg caps looking UP at 15 deg while looking down keeps 30. Not taste: ASimWorldCaptureActor refuses to write a frame whose depth channel is entirely invalid and calls Finish, and pitching up on a street empties it - measured 35.5% of the frame valid at pitch 0, 3.6% at 20 deg, zero at 27.5, which ended a capture 97519 frames in. A single 20 h episode has no checkpoint, so this cap matters more here than it did there.
body_note: Tokyo's own values. 6 cm is a step offset - a capsule resting exactly on the floor reports a hit at distance 0 - and 90 cm is the corridor clearance that produced Tokyo's 1065 m network, 0 collisions and a depth probe whose nearest reading was 85.2 cm. On rolling terrain inside a CORE these are not enough (WinterTown: 989 collisions, 20% of the network kept), which is documented in FINDINGS.md - but this profile does not walk cores.
reroute_note: MAX_REROUTE_ATTEMPTS defaults to 4 and is left on: it costs nothing when a route is already clean, and it is what turns a blocked place into a different road rather than a refused map.
yaw_note: yaw_deg_per_s pins the rotation rate (no per-episode draw from yaw_tier; the tier is kept for the 1.5x gate and metadata). turn_profile constant: every turning frame rotates exactly 45/24 deg, no ramp. The SAME rate and profile apply to looking up and down and to the return to level: _pitch_to shares _rotation_profile with turn(). Heading changes while walking a curved road are path-following and stay below the rate; where a corner would exceed it the walk stops and turns at the rate.
render_note: 17 Sep: TAA 2x is the global default by the user's decision (fewer motion flashes, ~23% lower sharpness proxy than TSR 2x; measurements in RENDER_QUALITY.md 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17 sections). r.AntiAliasingMethod 2 selects TAA; the history resolution, quality, frame weight, jitter samples, denser Lumen probes, fog grid, anisotropy, mip bias and sharpen cvars are the former stability_detail_candidate set. history_mode 4 (unchanged since 16 Sep) explicitly enables the capture TemporalAA show flag, keeps its view state and renders 32 warmup frames at pose 0 - a cvar alone falls back to FXAA because SceneCapture defaults TemporalAA=false. RGB is rendered 2x (2560x1440 -> 1280x720); depth stays native, no temporal AA or filtering. The previous TSR 2x default is kept verbatim in tasks/tsr_2x_previous_default.json for per-map comparison; a fallback to it must be written into the batch manifest, never switched silently. The render.taa field is a label only: nothing reads it, the cvars decide. Rebuild the native module before using mode 4; capture_engine logs every cvar it applied and the actor logs the TemporalAA show flag and warmup count.
retrace_note: 转身折返：转 180 度、沿刚走过的路正向走一段、再转回来继续。与 backward 不同 —— backward 是脸朝原方向、身体倒着走，画面还是已经看过的那一面；折返是把同一段路用相反的视角再看一遍，这正是空间记忆数据要的『重访』。节奏按中位数给：每次事件结束后抽一个目标间隔（中位数 median_interval_s，上下浮动 interval_jitter），max_interval_s 是兜底上限。给下界会让每个间隔都贴着下界，所以这里不设下界。min_duration_s 是往回走那一段的最短时长，身后的路不够长时宁可推迟到下一段也不缩水。
speed_note: 17 Sep: speed_m_s pins the walking pace at 1.0 m/s for every walking primitive - forward, backward, retreat and both retrace legs - instead of each style drawing a pace inside speed_tier (which is kept for the speed_within_tier gate). speed_profile constant: every walking frame moves exactly 100/24 cm, the last frame of a segment takes the remainder, no acceleration ramps. The mix tuner loses its speed lever when the pace is pinned; it keeps the other five.
passes_note: 17 Sep: every map is walked TWICE and that is the episode - target_passes 2, no wall-clock cap (max_duration_s 0 = however long two passes take). The two passes differ on purpose: pass 1 is the COVERING pass - one randomised cover of every road, the `styles` list rotating every 45 m, paced to finish within 97% of its budget (optional look/scan/retreat actions yield when it falls behind). Pass 2 is the FILL pass - a fresh covering walk from where pass 1 ended, every road again in a different order, walked entirely in fill_styles[0] (`study`: 2.5-5 m chunks, 30% backward, 35% retreat, look 100%, scan 90%, long holds) with no pace constraint. Retrace, speed and turn rate are the same in both. Pass 2 costs about 2x pass 1 (same distance, twice the action density), so an episode is ~3x the one-pass estimate; Tokyo measured consecutive passes at ~4x and ~8x the pure tour. The former rule (8 passes or 20 h, 5 h shards) was dropped by the user. gen_shards.py writes a per-map max_duration_s only as a runaway guard (2x the three-pass-equivalent estimate), never as a target.
styles_note: Pass 1 rotates these every 45 m of route. fill_styles: pass 2 uses fill_styles[0], pass 3 (if ever) fill_styles[1], and so on.
content_note: 17 Sep, user: 'only record where there is something'. content_buffer_m keeps only walkable ground within this distance of CONTENT before the centreline is thinned; the rest of a large empty level is dropped and the region is still chosen by (post-buffer) centreline length. content_mode 'dense' = survey_core's density core (>=6% obstacle within 12 m: a street between buildings, a grove, a yard of props) plus any footprint of 20 m2 or more; 'buildings' = footprints of 20 m2 or more only, so forests and rock fields count as empty. Measured at 10 m: ForestGasStation 1638 -> 585 m (dense) / 532 m (buildings); Mountains_Map 4619 -> 1282 / 317; Arctic 3617 -> 2892 / 1554; Tokyo 1144 -> 1003 / 979 (all streets, barely trimmed). Softer than confine_to_core, which kept only the built-up interior and needed 60/120 cm clearances to pass; this keeps the streets along the content on both sides. Set 0 to disable.
